reason: The hypothesis directly transfers the Sn addition strategy and its mechanism (Sn-rich interlayer as oxygen diffusion barrier) from well-studied Nb-silicide based alloys to the chemically and structurally distinct equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr RHEA, without providing a new mechanistic link or resolving the known conflict that Sn suppresses pesting but not spallation at higher temperatures; the proposal essentially restates the prior findings as a prediction for a new alloy.
copied_elements: adding 5 at.% Sn to suppress pest oxidation
formation of Sn-rich interfacial layer (Nb3Sn, Nb5Sn2Si, NbSn2) as diffusion barrier
improved scale adhesion and reduced weight gain
concern about spallation at high temperature
